limitations: Synthetic, author-labeled corpus; no independent expert validation.
Recall is measured per playbook rule, not every possible legal issue.
Exact quotations verify provenance, not interpretation or completeness.
Provider failures count as missed expected rules; they are not discarded.

findings.title: Liability Cap and Exclusion of Indirect Damages
findings.quote: The buyer's aggregate liability has no financial limit and includes loss of anticipated profit and other consequential loss.
findings.rationale: The clause does not cap liability at fees paid in the preceding 12 months and includes indirect damages, which deviates from the preference.
findings.proposed_language: The buyer's aggregate liability shall be capped at the fees paid in the preceding 12 months, and shall exclude any indirect, consequential, or special damages.

findings.title: Automatic Renewal Cancellation Deadline Exceeds 60 Days
findings.quote: To prevent automatic renewal for another year, the customer must deliver written cancellation no later than seventy-five days before the current term ends.
findings.rationale: The requirement for cancellation notice is seventy-five days, which exceeds the acceptable limit of sixty days, thus deviating from the preference for a cancellation deadline of sixty days or fewer.
findings.proposed_language: To prevent automatic renewal for another year, the customer must deliver written cancellation no later than sixty days before the current term ends.

findings.title: Supplier convenience termination notice period is insufficient.
findings.quote: The supplier may end this agreement for convenience on fourteen days of written notice and will refund all unused prepaid fees.
findings.rationale: The notice period of fourteen days does not meet the required minimum of thirty days for supplier convenience termination.
findings.proposed_language: The supplier may end this agreement for convenience on at least thirty days of written notice and will refund all unused prepaid fees.

findings.title: Data deletion period exceeds preference
findings.quote: Cobalt will erase the customer's data within twenty days after the service ends.
findings.rationale: The data deletion period of twenty days does not comply with the preference for deletion within thirty days of termination.
findings.proposed_language: Cobalt will erase the customer's data within thirty days after the service ends and will provide notice of any subprocessors.

findings.title: Lack of subprocessor notice
findings.quote: Cobalt may appoint subprocessors without informing the customer.
findings.rationale: The clause allows Cobalt to appoint subprocessors without informing the customer, which does not comply with the requirement for notice of subprocessors.
findings.proposed_language: Cobalt must inform the customer of any subprocessors it appoints.

findings.title: Unilateral Indemnity
findings.quote: Customer must indemnify Supplier for all claims connected with the service, including claims caused by Supplier's negligence; Supplier owes no indemnity to Customer.
findings.rationale: The clause imposes a unilateral indemnity obligation on the Customer without providing reciprocal indemnity from the Supplier, which deviates from the preference for appropriately scoped reciprocal indemnities.
findings.proposed_language: Both parties shall indemnify each other for claims arising from their respective negligence, misconduct, or breach of this agreement.
